## Taking stock: State of the project (11/10/2026)
I think its worth taking stock of where the project is, and what needs to happen next. 
Thus far the project has:

1. Build initial simulation utility inc analytical/plotting methods, examined the toy model, and validated it against analytical thermalization:
	* Adapted the provided simulation code for a fermionic quantum "star geometry" system-bath setup into a python code utility
	* Built various plotting methods into this code utility
	* Examined the simulation for a variety of input parameters
	* Implemented an analytical thermalization utility which predicts the thermalized system occupancy the simulation is expected to reach
2. Build the dual-simulation and dynamic map extraction utility:
	* Setup a dualSimulation class which runs simulations from empty/occupied initial states respectively
	* Extracted the dynamic map as outlined above
	* Compare the simulation results to a dynamic map propagated system occupancy - this revealed a typo in the dynamic map extraction step outlined above
	* Fixed the dynamic map extraction such that it agrees w/simulation
	* Implement some minor plotting utilities
3. Familiarise self w/theory for memory kernel definition:
	* Read parts of [@OpenQuantumSystemsIntro2012] which introduced the Nakajima-Zwansig formalism
	* considered how to extract the memory kernel
	* Read parts of multiple other papers before settling on the Transfer Tensor Method (TTM) as the most promising approach
	* Considered gaps in knowledge for this method, particularly when it comes to bounding the finite timestep error
